requirement:
A bundled skill MAY put material needed only in specialized situations in files it links to. Each such link MUST say when to read the file. Each bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, is a site:

:::{sites} skills
```yaml
language: markdown
paths: [assets/skills]
rule:
  kind: minus_metadata
match:
  - "---\nname: example\n---\n\n# Example\n"
no_match:
  - "# Example\n"
```
:::
rationale:
**Obligations.** The only MUST is "each such link MUST say when to read the file". The MAY imposes nothing to check. Each bundled skill upholds the MUST on its own, so each is a site and needs no `{impl}` reference. No obligation falls outside what the sites cover.

**Site query.** I ran `requirements.cli.skill_conventions.references/skills`. It matched the front matter of exactly five files:
- `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md`
- `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md`
- `assets/skills/habeas-evidence/SKILL.md`
- `assets/skills/habeas-refactor/SKILL.md`
- `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md`

Those are all five skill directories under `assets/skills`. A search for `---` lines in `assets/skills` found front matter only in these five. The `references/*.md` files have none, so they are rightly not sites. I found no skill that the query misses and no place outside the scope that it selects.

**Snippets.** The `match` snippet has front matter with a name and a heading. The `no_match` snippet is the same body without front matter. That shows what the `minus_metadata` rule selects and what it must not select, which is adequate for this single-condition query. The requirement has no violation queries.

**Tests.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bundled_skills_say_when_to_read_each_reference_file]` carries a `{test}` reference to the subject. For every skill in `SKILLS`, it iterates the skill's files other than `SKILL.md`. It asserts that each has an entry in the `links` table. It also asserts that the skill text, whitespace-collapsed, contains the "when to read" sentence for each entry. A new reference file with no listed link would fail the test.

I found no gaps.
